Implemented in worktree ../ac-satisfiability, pushed as Gerrit change 1021 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1021).

Plan review took 3 rounds; both BLOCKs were G1G2 omitted-site findings. The roster-building expression turned out to be duplicated in THREE places (pass1.py:154, fidelity_spot_eval.py:219, eval_solver.py:117), not one — so the fix single-sources it via pass1.build_sibling_roster rather than updating copies. Leaving the two eval harnesses on title-only rosters would have corrupted the dogfooding data G3's deferred posture decision rests on.

Local gates: make lint clean, make typecheck clean, pytest tests/unit = 5793 passed / 19 skipped / 0 failed. 20 new tests across test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py and test_container_roster.py.

Two pinned registries required deliberate updates: test_prompt_front_matter's canonical fixed-point round-trip (front matter canonicalized) and test_threshold_recalibration's full routing-table pin (ac-satisfiability added as advisory 0.95 — the pin exists to catch a silent posture flip). G3's posture/threshold left unchanged per scope.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan review certified epic `1386-5e7c-391d-4a74` and two of its children with zero blocking
findings even though acceptance criteria across them were mutually unsatisfiable. Every
contradiction surfaced later — mid-implementation or at the completion-verifier close gate —
and each correction forced a full LLM re-review because amending a description invalidates the
attestation as `stale-material`. Bug `creamy-cocksure-elkhound` records the evidence (seven
instances in four failure classes). Until this lands, every plan author and every agent claiming
a ticket keeps paying that late-detection cost.

## Approach

Two defects with two separate causes. They ship as one story because the second one's proving
tests instantiate the container pass that the first one's registration also touches, so splitting
them would duplicate that fixture and force one of the two to re-review against the other's
change to `pass1.py`.

**(1) A new 1-TURN criterion `ac-satisfiability` (facet `coherence`).** It owns a concern no
criterion owns today: whether a ticket's own acceptance criteria and its Scope / Out-of-Scope
declarations can all hold at once. `COH` covers contradictions BETWEEN sections and explicitly
disclaims within-section ones ("not within-section nitpicks (those belong to E1/E2)"); `E1`
covers criterion-to-description mapping, terminology and duplicates; `F1` covers measurability.
None asks whether the commitments are jointly satisfiable.

The rubric is written on a generic primitive rather than the motivating epic's subject matter:
*an acceptance criterion quantifies over a set — universally ("no file under X matches P") or by
cardinality ("the N items are migrated") — and something else in the same description places a
member inside the excepted region.* It names three shapes of that primitive:
universal-vs-carve-out (a Scope or Out-of-Scope clause exempts a member of the set an AC
quantifies over); derived-artifact closure (an AC asserts a property of an artifact the plan
says is regenerated from a source that keeps carrying the negation); and snapshot cardinality
(an AC pins a count measured at authoring time for a set the plan says is discovered or
recomputed at execution time).

Pass-2 already grades exactly this defect: `internal_conflict` is a live verifier axis
(`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py:255`) and a member of `_PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES`
(`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:309`). So the gap is confined to Pass-1 finding, and no
verifier or impact-model change is part of this work. The criterion ships `advisory` at the
`0.95` default; choosing a blocking posture needs replay data this change does not have yet.

Rejected: widening `COH` instead. It needs no new routing entry, but it puts two concerns in one
single-turn scan and erases the boundary the rubrics police out loud. A separate routed
criterion is also close to free: `registry.chunk_by_facet`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:434`) facet-sorts the single-turn tier then slices it
into fixed-size chunks, so chunk count is `ceil(total / n)` and one added criterion changes the
call count only when the applicable population is already an exact multiple of `n`. Single-turn
chunks are never shed by the per-plan budget cap, so it cannot be starved on a large ticket the
way an AGENT-tier alternative could.

**(2) Make `G3`'s child-coverage audit able to fire.** `G3` asks whether the union of children
covers each parent acceptance criterion, and `plan_review_container.md` instructs it to flag an
absence "only if NO sibling in the roster covers it". But the roster it is handed carries ids
and titles only, which cannot discharge that burden, so the anti-false-positive rule correctly
silences the finding every time. Give the roster each child's acceptance-criteria items,
extracted with `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` (`src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py:96`) — the same
helper the DET floor uses — and say so in `G3`'s rubric.

*Single-source the builder.* That roster is currently built by three independent copies of the
same expression — every caller of `passes.pass1_container` that is not a test rolls its own:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:154` — the production path;
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:219` — the spot-eval harness, feeding it in
  at lines 251 and 260;
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:117-119` — the eval-fixture solver, where the expression
  is the fallback behind a `case.get("sibling_roster")` fixture override.

Changing only the production copy would leave the two eval paths sending title-only rosters while
production sends AC-bearing ones. That matters beyond tidiness: those harnesses are what would
generate the dogfooding data for `G3`'s deferred posture decision, so the divergence would
corrupt the evidence for the next step. Extract one `build_sibling_roster(children)` helper and
call it from all three.

It goes in `pass1.py`: that module already owns roster construction, it has ample room under the
800-LOC cap, and both other callers can reach it with no new import edge — `eval_solver.py:98`
already does `from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, so the helper joins an
import that exists. Rejected putting it in `passes.py`, which at 781 lines is too close to the cap
to absorb a new helper. `eval_solver`'s `case.get("sibling_roster")` override stays ahead of the
helper, so a fixture can still pin a roster verbatim.

*The rendered format.* `build_sibling_roster` emits one block per child: the existing
`- <ticket_id>: <title>` line, followed by that child's `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items`
entries each on its own line indented two spaces under it. A child with no parseable acceptance
criteria keeps its `- <id>: <title>` line alone, so the roster degrades to today's shape rather
than dropping the child. `G3`'s rubric refers to these indented items as the child's acceptance
criteria.

*Where the roster is sent.* The roster is byte-identical across every pairing of one review, but
it currently sits in `instructions` AFTER the per-pairing `children_block`, so it can never be
part of a stable prefix. Fattening it in place would re-send the whole child
acceptance-criteria corpus once per pairing, growing with the square of the child count. Instead
send it once in the byte-stable prefix: in `passes.pass1_container`, build the system prompt as
`_resolve_system(PASS_CONTAINER, parent_plan, cfg)` concatenated with a rendered roster block,
and delete the roster from `instructions`. This is plain string concatenation on the already
resolved system prompt — `_resolve_system` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:276`) keeps its
current `(prompt_id, plan, cfg)` signature, `plan_review_container.md` gains no new template
variable, and the roster stays a runtime value. In `passes.py` this is a move, not an addition:
the roster leaves `instructions` as it joins the system prompt, holding that file flat against
the cap.

*Count the roster in the prefix budget.* `parent_tokens` (`pass1.py:156`) is estimated from the
parent plan alone, and it feeds three decisions: container bin-packing
(`sizing.pack_container_bins`, `pass1.py:166`), the per-pairing size estimate (`pass1.py:168`),
and the warm-then-fan-out gate `parent_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (`pass1.py:48`, `:187`).
Once the roster is part of the prefix, it must be included in that estimate or bins can be packed
over the window budget. Add it to the estimate.

Note the honest limit of the caching claim: sending the roster once in a byte-stable prefix makes
it *cacheable* and stops it being re-sent per pairing, but whether a cache is actually written
still depends on the prefix clearing `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (4096) and on there being at least
two pairings. A larger prefix makes that gate more likely to pass, not less. The acceptance
criteria below therefore assert the structural property (the roster is sent in the prefix, once,
not repeated in per-pairing instructions), which is deterministic and testable, rather than a
cache-hit rate.

Rejected for (2): making the new criterion agentic so it fetches siblings itself. Cross-child
contradiction is already `G4`'s declared concern, so that would duplicate an owned concern and
force AGENT cost onto the cheap check. `G3`'s posture and threshold are deliberately left
untouched — revisiting them needs dogfooding data from this change.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_ac_satisfiability.md` — new: the criterion rubric
  (prompt id `plan-review-ac-satisfiability`, per the stem-underscores-to-dashes convention in
  `prompts._packaged_prompt_files`).
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` — rubric: discharge the sibling test against the
  roster's acceptance criteria.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `ac-satisfiability` routing entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `ac-satisfiability` to `CANONICAL_LLM`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the shared `build_sibling_roster` helper; include the
  roster in the `parent_tokens` prefix estimate.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` — call the shared helper instead of its own
  copy of the roster expression.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` — call the shared helper as the fallback behind its
  existing `sibling_roster` fixture override.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — move the roster from `instructions` into the system
  prompt.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated from the registry.
- `tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py` — new.
- `tests/unit/test_container_roster.py` — new.

## Testing

- Happy path: with `ac-satisfiability` registered, `validate_packaged_routing()` returns an
  empty list and `chunk_by_facet` places it in the facet-sorted `coherence` group alongside
  `COH` and `E1`.
- Happy path: the roster built for a parent whose children carry `## Acceptance Criteria`
  sections contains each child's criterion text.
- Wiring, end to end through Pass-1: drive the single-turn chunk path with a `FakeRunner`
  (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:111`) and assert the new criterion reaches the finder rubric and that
  a finding it emits survives criterion-attribution validation. This proves the criterion is
  actually wired into a review rather than only registered; judging its LLM accuracy is what the
  deferred dogfooding pass is for.
- Edge: a child whose description has no `## Acceptance Criteria` section yields a roster entry
  without raising.
- Empty: a parent with no children yields an empty roster without raising.
- Contract: all three non-test callers of `pass1_container` obtain their roster from the one
  shared builder, so they cannot diverge.
- Contract: `eval_solver`'s `sibling_roster` fixture override still wins over the builder.
- Happy path: the rendered roster puts each child's acceptance-criteria items indented under its
  `- <id>: <title>` line.
- Contract: the container pass sends the roster in its system prompt and not in its per-pairing
  instructions.
- Regression: the existing plan-review unit suite stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ac-satisfiability` is a registered plan-review criterion routed as `exec: "1-TURN"`,
      `facet: "coherence"`, `default_posture: "advisory"`; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_routing_entry` and by
      `validate_packaged_routing()` returning an empty list.
- [ ] Its rubric states the set-quantification primitive and names all three contradiction
      shapes (universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, snapshot cardinality), and does
      not reference the `Success Criteria` migration that motivated it; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_rubric_is_generic`.
- [ ] The criterion is exercised end to end through the Pass-1 single-turn chunk path against a
      `FakeRunner`, and a finding it emits survives attribution validation; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_reaches_pass1_and_attributes`.
- [ ] `explain_criterion("ac-satisfiability")` returns the criterion's non-empty guide section
      rather than raising `ExplainError`; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_explain_returns_section`.
- [ ] Nothing under `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/` changes, because Pass-2's
      `internal_conflict` axis already grades this defect; verified by
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/` exiting 0.
- [ ] The sibling roster carries each child's acceptance-criteria items, not only ids and titles;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_carries_child_ac`.
- [ ] All three non-test callers of `pass1_container` (`pass1.py`, `fidelity_spot_eval.py`,
      `eval_solver.py`) obtain the roster from the single shared `build_sibling_roster` helper,
      and none retains its own roster-building expression; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_builder_single_sourced`.
- [ ] `eval_solver`'s `sibling_roster` fixture override still takes precedence over the shared
      builder; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_eval_fixture_roster_override_wins`.
- [ ] The rendered roster places each child's acceptance-criteria items indented beneath that
      child's `- <id>: <title>` line, and a child with no parseable criteria keeps its line
      alone; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_render_format`.
- [ ] A child description with no `## Acceptance Criteria` section, and a parent with no
      children, each produce a roster without raising; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_degrades_gracefully`.
- [ ] `G3`'s rubric instructs the reviewer to test "no sibling covers it" against the roster's
      acceptance criteria; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_g3_rubric_cites_roster_ac`.
- [ ] The container pass sends the roster inside its system prompt and not inside its
      per-pairing instructions; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_rides_prefix_not_instructions`.
- [ ] The roster's token cost is included in the `parent_tokens` prefix estimate that feeds
      container bin-packing and the warm gate; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_counted_in_prefix_estimate`.
- [ ] `G3`'s `default_posture` and `block_threshold` are unchanged from their pre-change values;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_g3_posture_unchanged`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` parity-checks clean against the registry; verified by
      `validate_criteria_guide()` returning an empty list.
- [ ] No `src/rebar/**/*.py` file exceeds the 800-LOC cap; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/unit` all pass.
